standard.title: Evaluate perspective representation through language
standard.description: analyse and evaluate how language features are used to represent a perspective of an issue, event, situation, individual or group
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse how language features shape meaning and vary according to audience and purpose (AC9E7LY03). They have not yet evaluated language features as perspective-representing devices — moving from describing what features do to evaluating how effectively they represent a perspective.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how language features represent perspectives on issues, events, situations, individuals or groups.

nodes.label: Language features as perspective devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how specific language features represent a perspective — identifying the choices and explaining the perspective they embed.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two language features in a text and analyse how each represents a particular perspective on the text's subject.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how language features across a text work together to represent a perspective — examining how language in news and social media coverage of a contentious issue is used to convey opinions and represent ideas.
wider: Compare language features across coverage of the same contentious issue in two media contexts with different editorial positions
Examine how language features in inspirational or advocacy speeches position the audience toward a perspective — identifying techniques that influence listener response

response_modes.reason: Perspective representation is easiest to see in obviously biased texts. Students need to encounter subtler uses — in news reporting, in ostensibly neutral descriptions — to understand that all language represents perspective, not just intentionally persuasive texts.

success_criteria: Student identifies a language feature and names the perspective it represents
Student explains how the feature represents the perspective — not just that it 'shows the author's opinion'
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluating representation at N2 requires being able to identify which language features represent a perspective and how — students who haven't built this analytical move have no basis for evaluative judgement beyond personal agreement or disagreement.

nodes.label: Evaluating perspective representation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how effectively or fairly language features represent a perspective — making and supporting judgements about language choices as representational tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one language choice as a representation tool — making a judgement about whether it represents the perspective fairly, effectively or misleadingly, and supporting the judgement with evidence.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate how language features are used to represent perspectives across a range of text types — comparing campaign speeches, journalism and social media, and making supported judgements about the effectiveness and fairness of representational choices.
wider: Evaluate how language in a historical text represents a group in ways that are now recognised as problematic, and assess the impact of such representations
Examine advocacy speeches from films or media and evaluate how language features influence the listener — assessing both effectiveness and ethical dimensions of the techniques used

response_modes.reason: Evaluating language representation requires criteria for judgement — students need reasoning scaffolds for what makes a representation fair, effective or misleading. Without criteria, evaluation collapses into agreement or disagreement with the perspective rather than analysis of the representation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The evaluative dimension — assessing fairness and effectiveness — connects language analysis to media literacy and civic capability. Advancing students can engage with the ethical dimensions of representation, which is substantive width within Year 9 scope.
success_criteria: Student makes a supported evaluative judgement about a language choice as a representation tool
Student's evaluation goes beyond agreeing or disagreeing with the perspective — it assesses how the language works as representation
